# Numerous cases of hantavirus identified aboard luxury cruise MV Hondius. Seven cases of hantavirus have been identified after a suspected outbreak on a luxury cruise ship off West Africa that has killed three people. The World Health Organization says there are two confirmed cases and five suspected cases on the ship, carrying mostly British, American and Spanish passengers. “As of May 4, 2026, seven cases (two laboratory confirmed cases of hantavirus and five suspected cases) have been identified, including three deaths, one critically ill patient and three individuals reporting mild symptoms,” the WHO said. About 150 people are still stuck on the vessel after a Dutch couple and a German national died, and others fell ill, including a Briton who left the vessel and was being treated in South Africa, authorities said. Medics were working on Monday to evacuate two people with symptoms of the virus. The Netherlands’ National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM), which is assisting with the outbreak, said hantavirus had been confirmed in one of the patients showing symptoms. But authorities in the island nation of Cape Verde said they had not allowed Dutch-flagged MV Hondius to dock as a precaution. Oceanwide Expeditions was trying to arrange the repatriation of two crew members with symptoms of the disease — one British and one Dutch — along with the body of the German national and a “guest closely associated with the deceased” who does not have symptoms. Spanish authorities said they had not yet received a request for the ship to dock and disembark passengers there. South Africa’s Health Department confirmed two of the dead were Dutch nationals: a 70-year-old man, who died on St Helena on April 11, and his wife, 69, who died in South Africa after collapsing at OR Tambo International Airport.

Title: Hantavirus on Cruise Ship MV Hondius
# 7 Suspected Hantavirus Cases Aboard Cruise Ship MV Hondius. A serious public health incident is unfolding aboard the cruise vessel MV Hondius in the Atlantic Ocean, where seven suspected cases of hantavirus have been reported—including three deaths and one British passenger currently in intensive care, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of these cases, two have been confirmed through laboratory testing; the remaining five are under investigation to determine whether they are linked. ## Ship Held Off Cape Verde Amid Quarantine. The MV Hondius remains anchored off the coast of Cape Verde, under quarantine. Local authorities have prohibited passenger disembarkation to protect public health. Oceanwide Expeditions, the operator of the vessel, described the situation as controlled and noted that the atmosphere onboard remains calm, with most passengers staying composed. ## ‘We Just Want to Go Home’. American passenger Jake Rosmarin shared a powerful video on social media, appealing for empathy and support. Speaking to his roughly 44,000 followers, he emphasized the human reality behind the headlines: “We’re not just a news story or a headline. We’re people—with families and lives waiting for us back home.” He described mounting psychological strain, citing uncertainty as the hardest part. “All we want is to feel safe, to get clear answers—and to go home.” He closed his message by asking for “kindness and understanding” from those following the situation. ## About Hantavirus. Hantavirus is typically transmitted to humans through contact with rodent droppings, saliva, or urine. Among the three fatalities reported so far are a Dutch couple and a German passenger; it has not yet been confirmed whether all deaths were caused by hantavirus. A 69-year-old British man is hospitalized in critical but stable condition at a hospital in South Africa, where infection with a hantavirus variant has been confirmed. Additionally, two crew members are exhibiting acute respiratory symptoms and require urgent medical attention—though the cause remains unconfirmed. Authorities are also considering relocating the ship to the Canary Islands to facilitate safe disembarkation and comprehensive medical evaluations. The WHO is closely monitoring developments and collaborating with national and regional health authorities to support the epidemiological investigation. News about Greece and the World.
